message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough.  
Feel free to skip sections you already know or dive deeper into any part.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| **1** | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office work). | List required specs: CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, PSU, case, cooling. |
| **2** | **Gather Parts** | All components must be compatible. | Use a PC builder tool (e.g., PCPartPicker) to check compatibility and price. |
| **3** | **Prepare Workspace** | Clean, static‑free area. | Anti‑static wrist strap or mat; keep parts away from metal surfaces. |
| **4** | **Open the Case** | Access motherboard, power supply, drives. | Remove side panels, unscrew screws, set aside. |
| **5** | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power to all components. | Align with rear exhaust, screw in, route cables. |
| **6** | **Mount the Motherboard** | Base for all other components. | Align standoffs, screw in, leave ports exposed. |
| **7** | **Install the CPU** | Central processing unit. | Open socket latch, align CPU, gently place, lock latch. |
| **8** | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install CPU Cooler** | Keeps CPU temperature low. | Use a pea‑size amount, spread evenly, attach cooler. |
| **9** | **Insert RAM Modules** | Memory for multitasking. | Slot into DIMM slots, click until secure. |
| **10** | **Mount Storage Drives (SSD/HDD)** | Primary data storage. | Mount SSD in M.2 slot or 2.5” bay; HDD in 3.5” bay. |
| **11** | **Install the Graphics Card (GPU)** | Handles rendering for games, video, etc. | Insert into PCI‑e x16 slot, secure with screws, connect power cables. |
| **12** | **Connect Power Cables** | Power all components. | PSU 24‑pin to motherboard, 8‑pin CPU, GPU power, SATA power to drives. |
| **13** | **Connect Data Cables** | Data transfer between components. | SATA data to drives, M.2 cable if needed, USB headers to front panel. |
| **14** | **Attach Front Panel Connectors** | Power button, reset, LEDs, USB ports. | Refer to motherboard manual for exact pin layout. |
| **15** | **Cable Management** | Improves airflow, aesthetics. | Tidy cables with ties or Velcro straps, route through cable grommets. |
| **16** | **Close the Case** | Protect components, finish look. | Reattach side panels, screw in. |
| **17** | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | Verify hardware, set boot order. | Press power button, enter BIOS (usually F2/Del), check component detection. |
| **18** | **Install Operating System (OS)** | Turn your PC into a usable machine. | Create bootable USB (Windows, Linux), install OS, update drivers. |
| **19** | **Install Drivers & Software** | Ensure optimal performance. | Download latest GPU, chipset, audio drivers; install essential software. |
| **20** | **Test & Benchmark** | Confirm stability, performance. | Run stress tests (Prime95, FurMark), benchmark (Cinebench, 3DMark). |

---

#### Quick Checklist

- **CPU** – Intel i5/i7/i9 or AMD Ryzen 5/7/9
- **Motherboard** – ATX, micro‑ATX, or mini‑ITX with matching socket
- **RAM** – 16 GB DDR4/DDR5 (minimum)
- **Storage** – NVMe SSD (250 GB+) + optional HDD
- **GPU** – NVIDIA RTX 3060/3070 or AMD RX 6600/6700
- **PSU** – 550–750 W, 80+ Gold
- **Case** – Mid‑tower or mini‑tower with good airflow
- **Cooling** – Stock cooler or aftermarket air/liquid cooler

---

#### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Short circuits** | Use anti‑static wrist strap; double‑check cable routing. |
| **Component not detected** | Verify proper seating, check BIOS updates. |
| **Overheating** | Ensure adequate airflow, clean dust filters. |
| **Power issues** | Double‑check PSU wattage, use a reputable brand. |
| **Driver conflicts** | Install only one GPU driver set; remove old ones. |

---

#### Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build & compare parts, check compatibility.  
- **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware.  
- **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community help.  
- **Manuals** – Keep motherboard, PSU, and case manuals handy.

---

### Final Thought

Building a PC is a rewarding project that gives you full control over performance and aesthetics. Take your time, follow the steps carefully, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for more detailed help on any specific step. Happy building!
